quiz.prompt: `git revert` vs `git reset --hard` on a pushed commit:
options: revert adds a new undoing commit, safe for shared history
quiz.explain: revert records a new commit that undoes the old one, so others' history stays intact; reset --hard rewrites history.

options: Two branches change the same lines differently
quiz.explain: Git merges automatically unless both sides edited the same lines (or one deleted what the other changed).

options: A movable pointer to a commit
quiz.explain: A branch is just a named reference to a commit that moves forward as you commit; no files are copied.
stash saves uncommitted changes and cleans the working tree; `git stash pop` brings them back.

quiz.prompt: When would you rebase instead of merge, and when must you never rebase?
rubric: Rebase to keep a linear history of local/feature work
Never rebase commits others already pulled (shared/public)

capstone.title: Reproducible project kit
capstone.brief: (8h) A GitHub template repo every later project starts from: uv project (src layout, lockfile); Ruff, mypy, pytest + coverage; pre-commit; GitHub Actions matrix; .env.example + 12-factor settings loader; multi-stage non-root Dockerfile + compose with Postgres; Makefile setup/test/lint/run; issue/PR templates; README 'recreate from zero in 5 commands'. Reviewer clones on a fresh machine. Also required: Learn Git Branching Introduction + Ramping Up and Bandit level 20. Pass ≥8/10.

rubric.criterion: Reproducibility (fresh clone → tests pass in ≤5 commands)
CI gates (lint, type, test; main protected)
Git hygiene (issues → PRs → reviews; meaningful history; one resolved conflict)
Secrets & config (none in history; .env.example; fails loudly)
